source_name: NBRNM — Fast money transfer transaction statistics
why_relevant: Volume/value series for remittance flows — sizes the non-bank transfer market that wallets and PSPs are trying to capture.

source_name: NBRNM — Payment statistics (Платежна статистика)
why_relevant: Card, POS, e-commerce and terminal statistics — the denominator for any claim about e-commerce acceptance growth and the origin of the widely cited 'active e-commerce sales points' figures.

source_name: NBRNM — Crypto-assets Q&A / regulatory position
why_relevant: Central bank's stated position on crypto-assets — determines whether crypto/e-money startups can legally operate or partner with MK banks.

source_name: Financial Intelligence Office of RNM (Управа за финансиско разузнавање)
why_relevant: AML rulebooks explicitly enumerate obliged entity classes including money remittance providers; national risk assessments describe the remittance and virtual-asset landscape and its actors.

source_name: AETM — Association for E-Commerce of Macedonia (ecommerce.mk)
why_relevant: Industry association publishing the national e-merchant register, annual e-commerce reports and payment-preference surveys; the richest single pointer to MK merchants, PSPs and acquiring banks.

source_name: AETM Register of e-merchants (Регистар на е-трговци)
why_relevant: Searchable list of MK e-merchants with integrated online card payment via one of the five acquiring banks — a direct proxy for who acquires whom in MK e-commerce.

source_name: eCommerce4all.mk — e-payment guide module
why_relevant: Donor/association-produced practitioner guide that names the local processor (CaSys/cPay), lists which MK banks do acquiring, and gives merchant onboarding costs — rare explicit mapping of the acquiring landscape.

source_name: cPay integration plugin listings (Holest, Vendor eCommerce and similar integrator blogs)
why_relevant: Third-party integrator docs expose cPay's technical interface, onboarding steps and fees — reveals gateway adoption among MK webshops and which platforms dominate.

source_name: Iute Pay / Iute Group North Macedonia
why_relevant: First non-bank EMI licensed in MK (July 2025) — wallet, cardless ATM, QR merchant payments; a listed-bond issuer so it publishes unusually detailed operational and partner disclosure.

source_name: Monri Payments North Macedonia (Payten group)
why_relevant: Regional PSP with an MK-localised site offering online payments and installment-at-checkout via partner banks — direct competitor/partner mapping for e-commerce acquiring.

source_name: Payten — group newsroom (regional acquirer/PSP consolidator, Skopje acquisitions)
why_relevant: Payten's M&A and product announcements (e.g. acquisition of Skopje-based Grouper, majority stake in Monri) show how the MK payments value chain is being consolidated by a regional player.

source_name: IT.mk and forum.it.mk — Macedonian tech media and fintech thread
why_relevant: Local tech press covering fintech launches, e-tolling payments, wallet rollouts; the long-running fintech forum thread is an informal but early aggregator of MK payments news and rumours.

source_name: Faktor.mk — business/finance news (e-money and fintech coverage)
why_relevant: Business daily that covers e-money licensing, wallet launches and bank-fintech deals in MK with named companies.

source_name: Pari.com.mk — MK financial news portal
why_relevant: Covers fintech marketing activity, product launches and partnerships (e.g. Iute Pay student innovation challenge) — useful for go-to-market and ecosystem-partnership signals.

source_name: Meta.mk — regulatory/tech policy reporting on payment services
why_relevant: Reports on NBRNM sub-laws enabling e-money and new payment services — useful for tracking when the regulatory gate opens for new challengers.

source_name: Bloomberg Adria (Macedonian edition) — fintech and crypto coverage
why_relevant: Regional business outlet comparing MK's e-money lag with Serbia/BiH and profiling regional challengers expanding into MK — good for cross-border competitor entry signals.

source_name: TheRecursive.com — SEE startup and fintech funding coverage (MK tag)
why_relevant: Covers Macedonian fintech startups, funding rounds and founders — the main English source for early-stage MK payments/investment startups before they appear in registers.

source_name: Mondaq — North Macedonia FinTech Comparative Guide (law firm chapters)
why_relevant: Law-firm authored jurisdiction guide describing licensing regimes, which activities require NBRNM vs Ministry of Finance authorisation, and constraints on non-bank entrants.

source_name: Small World FS blog — North Macedonia payments/SEPA commentary
why_relevant: A remittance operator publicly commenting on MK's payments reform and SEPA alignment — reveals how cross-border remittance players read the MK market.

source_name: Bank remittance-partner disclosure documents (e.g. Stopanska Banka Western Union general offer)
why_relevant: Bank T&C/offer PDFs name the remittance brand each bank represents as agent and the payment-initiation role it plays — a reliable way to reconstruct the remittance-operator/bank partnership map.

source_name: Bank digital-wallet product pages (NLB Pay, Komercijalna Banka mobile wallet, KomPay)
why_relevant: Incumbent wallet offers define the competitive baseline non-bank challengers must beat, and their tech pages often reveal the tokenisation/processing vendor behind them.

source_name: SeeNews - North Macedonia country channel (banking/deals/investments)
why_relevant: Regional SEE business newswire that systematically covers MK bank capital raises, IFI loans, tenders and payment-scheme milestones in English; individual items observed include TTK Banka capital increase, EBRD loans to ProCredit Bank, and 'North Macedonia registers four banks in SEPA credit transfer scheme'. Translates MK-only facts for foreign readers and time-stamps deal flow useful for competitor/partnership tracking.

source_name: European Commission - Enlargement package: North Macedonia country reports (SWD series)
why_relevant: Annual EC staff working documents assess Chapter 4/9 (financial services), payment services alignment (PSD2), AML, digital transformation and e-government in MK, with dated, citable statements of what legislation and infrastructure exists. Excellent baseline for regulatory drivers behind bank IT spend.

source_name: Ministry of European Affairs (MK) - Macedonian working translations of EC country reports
why_relevant: Hosts Macedonian-language working versions of the EC annual report; gives the authoritative MK terminology for EU financial-sector concepts (платежни услуги, финансиски услуги, дигитална трансформација) needed to build local-language query sets for other cells.

source_name: IMF - Republic of North Macedonia country page (Article IV staff reports, FSSA/PLL reviews)
why_relevant: Article IV staff reports and selected-issues annexes carry banking-sector structure data, digitalisation/fintech boxes, payment-system oversight commentary and AML/CFT assessments; the informational annexes list technical assistance and World Bank/IMF payments work that often precedes vendor procurement.

source_name: IMF eLibrary (staff country reports, full text)
why_relevant: Structured full-text/XML access to MK staff reports and informational annexes, easier to query than scattered PDFs; useful for longitudinal extraction of banking-sector indicators.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports - North Macedonia financial sector / payments
why_relevant: Policy notes and diagnostics quantify MK payments (e.g. remittance cost ~7% of transaction value) and financial inclusion; the Bank also runs electronic-payments-acceptance assessments jointly with the National Bank, which map the acquiring/POS landscape - directly relevant to vendor and competitor mapping.
